abstract: As bird calls weaken with distance, their recordings lose spectral detail. We examine how species recognition varies with distance using controlled playback of ten-second excerpts from 20 bird species at seven distances from 1 to 48 ft. An STM32-based recording system acquires and stores the audio, which is subsequently analyzed on a computer using acoustic measurements and BirdNET. Across four metadata configurations, mean-aggregated top-1 accuracy is 95--100% through 24 ft, 90--95% at 36 ft, and 80--90% at 48 ft, with 20 recordings evaluated per configuration at each distance. Across the screened recordings, the median upper spectral edge is below its 1-ft reference at every evaluated distance from 4 to 36 ft, indicating an overall reduction in upper-frequency content with distance. These results show that recognition remains high through 24 ft despite measurable spectral degradation, followed by greater and configuration-dependent losses at longer distances.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对短距离回放下声学退化是否转化为识别失效的问题，本研究用 20 个物种 7 个距离的 STM32 同录音配对声学测量与 BirdNET 评分，证实平均汇聚 top-1 准确率在 24 ft 内保持 95% 至 100% 而 48 ft 靠地点元数据才回升至 90%，代价是总功率已衰减约 44 dB 且谱统计子集在远距离急剧流失。
originalTitle: Bird-Call Recognition Across Distance: Acoustic Degradation and BirdNET Performance
readerTitle: 鸟鸣远距离识别与频谱退化的配对实证
